findings.text: non-blocking: the bound assertion reads bound from recovery_wait.WAIT_PROBE_RUN_BOUND_SECONDS and asserts that integer appears in the duty detail, and the detail is built from that same constant, so the two sides move together and the assertion holds whatever value the constant takes; an independent literal, or the elapsed measurement already taken at line 156, would give it a fixed side.

non-blocking: the sweep's reader is routed through the gate but no assertion fails if it is reverted to its own subprocess.run, and the observed='stopped' branch two lines below is never exercised by any test, so half of the landed change can regress silently while the file stays green.

non-blocking: WAIT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 1.0 no longer bounds any probe now that recovery_wait.py:808 replaces both readers' own timeboxes, so it survives only as a noqa re-export shim (recovery_wait.py:2063) and a reader comparing it with WAIT_PROBE_RUN_BOUND_SECONDS = 60.0 gets two different answers about one wait's probe.

non-blocking: the classifier's reader this call reaches was previously timeboxed at 1 s (WAIT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) and now runs against the gate's 60 s bound under an exclusive cross-node lock, so an acknowledgements or obligations view can block up to a minute on one slow probe where it was bounded at one second; the bound is the plan's number, but the widening on this hot path is not named in the goal.
